silicon-on-insulator (SOI) substrate comprising a silicon device layer disposed on a buried oxide (Box) layer. upper_row_ss: Preamble: "A multi-channel silicon photonic waveguide multiplexer comprising:"

Accused Product: LumiLink 800G-DR8 optical transceiver module, manufactured and sold by Lumicore Technologies, Inc. The LumiLink 800G-DR8 is an 800-gigabit intensity-modulated optical transceiver module utilizing eight lanes of 100G-per-lane PAM4 signaling. The module incorporates a silicon photonic integrated circuit that includes a multi-channel waveguide multiplexer for combining eight optical channels onto a reduced number of output waveguides for transmission over parallel single-mode fibers.Evidentiary Support: Benchmark teardown report for the LumiLink 800G-DR8 (June 2023) (Exhibit OWS-2001); annotated teardown photographs (Exhibits OWS-2002 through OWS-2058); Lumicore product datasheet for the LumiLink 800G-DR8 (LC-00005100 through LC-00005122); Dr. Michaud deposition testimony (November 19, 2024) at 71:5–73:14 (confirming the 800G-DR8 incorporates a silicon photonic IC with waveguide multiplexing functionality).Dr.Ashford's Explanation:The LumiLink 800G-DR8 contains a silicon photonic integrated circuit that includes a multi-channel waveguide multiplexer. Although the 800G-
lower_row_ss: DR8 employs eight wavelength channels (compared to four in the 400G-ZR+), the multiplexer architecture is functionally and structurally similar. The Benchmark teardown identifies two four-channel AWG multiplexers on the 800G-DR8 PIC, each combining four wavelength channels onto a single output waveguide, for a total of two output fibers carrying the aggregated 800G signal. To the extent the preamble is limiting, the LumiLink 800G-DR8 satisfies it.

upper_row_ss: "further comprising a star coupler at an output end of the phased array, the star coupler having a Rowland circle geometry with a radius R selected to minimize focal-point aberration for each of the plurality of distinct wavelengths."

Accused Element: The Benchmark teardown report (Exhibit OWS-1001 at pp. 40–41) identifies a star coupler structure (also referred to as the output slab coupler) at the output end of the phased array in the LumiLink 400G-ZR+ AWG. Annotated optical micrographs (Exhibit OWS-1015) show the star coupler region with a curved boundary conforming to a Rowland circle geometry, which is the standard design approach for AWG output couplers to minimize focal-point aberration. Lumicore design files (LC-HC-SC-00012225) include the output slab coupler layout with a Rowland circle radius (R) of approximately 145 μm, which Lumicore's simulation files (LC-HC-SC-00013015) confirm was optimized to minimize aberration across the CWDM4 wavelength band.Evidentiary Support: Benchmark teardown (Exhibit OWS-1001 at pp. 40–41); annotated photograph (Exhibit OWS-1015); Lumicore design files (LC-HC-SC-00012225); Lumicore simulation files (LC-HC-SC-00013015); Kevin Ng deposition (January 7, 2025) at 70:14–71:8 (confirming identification of the Rowland circle geometry).Dr.Ashford's Explanation: Claim 5 adds a star coupler with Rowland circle geometry at the output end of the phased array. The Benchmark teardown identifies this structure in the LumiLink 400G-ZR+ AWG, and the Lumicore design files confirm the Rowland circle geometry with a radius optimized for the product's wavelength channels. The Rowland circle design is the industry-standard approach for AWG output couplers, and its presence in the accused product is confirmed by both physical teardown evidence and design-file analysis.

"a coherent detection module integrated on the silicon substrate, the coherent detection module comprising a 90° optical hybrid, at least two pairs of balanced photodetectors, and a local oscillator input waveguide configured to receive light from a local oscillator laser source;"

Accused Element: The LumiLink 400G-ZR+ PIC includes a coherent detection module (coherent receiver) integrated on the SOI substrate, as identified by the Benchmark teardown (Exhibit OWS-1001 at pp. 52–58). The coherent receiver comprises: (i) a 90° optical hybrid implemented as a 4×4 MMI coupler (Exhibit OWS-1023); (ii) two pairs of balanced Ge-on-Si photodetectors (four photodetectors total, arranged in two balanced pairs for in-phase and quadrature detection) (Exhibits OWS-1024, OWS-1025); and (iii) a local oscillator (LO) input waveguide that receives light from an external narrow-linewidth tunable laser source coupled to the PIC via an edge coupler (Exhibit OWS-1026). Lumicore design files (LC-HC-SC-00012360 through LC-HC-SC-00012410) show the complete coherent receiver layout including the 90° hybrid, balanced photodetector pairs, and LO input waveguide. Dr. Michaud confirmed (November 19, 2024, at 82:18–85:6) that the LumiLink 400G-ZR+ uses a "standard coherent receiver architecture with a 90-degree hybrid and balanced detection." Note on Doctrine of Equivalents (Claims 3 and 7): For Claim 1, OWS asserts literal infringement of the "coherent detection module" limitation. For dependent Claims 3 and 7, which add further requirements to the coherent detection module, OWS also asserts infringement under the doctrine of equivalents. The function-way-result analysis for the doctrine of equivalents as applied to Claims 3 and 7 is presented in companion Appendix B.Dr. Ashford's Explanation: The LumiLink 400G-ZR+ contains a coherent detection module with every element recited in this limitation: the 90° optical hybrid, balanced photodetector pairs, and LO input waveguide are all integrated on the silicon substrate. The Benchmark teardown and Lumicore design files confirm the presence of each component.
